h1: Wills & Estate Planning Lawyer in El Paso
intro: Most El Paso adults are three documents away from protecting their family: a will, a durable power of attorney and a medical directive. Attorney Robert Navar prepares them for a flat fee, signs them with you in English or Spanish, and handles probate when the time comes.
summary: A Texas will under Estates Code Chapters 251–254 needs two witnesses and a self-proving affidavit; done right, it lets the family skip most of the courtroom.
Without a will, Texas intestacy rules decide who inherits — and in blended families the surviving spouse often does not get the whole house.
A durable power of attorney and medical directive cover you while you are alive but unable to act, which is the gap a will does nothing about.
Estates of $75,000 or less (excluding the homestead and exempt property) can often use a small estate affidavit instead of full probate. Flat fees are quoted after a free consultation.

sections.heading: The Core Documents Every El Paso Adult Should Have
paragraphs: Estate planning in El Paso is usually simpler than people fear. For most families it comes down to a short set of documents, each doing one job. The will names who gets what, who raises minor children, and who serves as executor; under Estates Code Chapter 251 it must be signed in front of two witnesses, and with a self-proving affidavit the witnesses never have to come to court later. We draft wills to allow independent administration under Chapter 401, which keeps the probate court's involvement to a minimum and is the single biggest time-saver for an El Paso family.

The durable power of attorney under Estates Code Chapters 751–752 lets someone you trust handle the bank, the mortgage and the bills if you are incapacitated. The medical power of attorney and directive to physicians under Health and Safety Code Chapter 166 let that person — or a different one — make treatment decisions and spell out your wishes about life support. These documents matter while you are alive; a will only takes effect after death. With a HIPAA release and beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and life insurance, that is a complete basic plan.

sections.heading: What Happens in El Paso Without a Will: Intestacy Surprises
paragraphs: When an El Paso resident dies without a will, the Texas Estates Code decides who inherits, and the answer surprises families constantly. Texas is a community-property state. If the deceased was married and all the children are also the surviving spouse's children, the spouse generally keeps the community property. But if there are children from a prior relationship — common in El Paso — the deceased's half of the community property passes to those children, not to the spouse. The surviving spouse can end up co-owning the home with stepchildren.

Separate property splits differently again, with the spouse taking a fraction and the children or the deceased's parents taking the rest. Unmarried partners inherit nothing. Minor children who inherit outright need a court-supervised guardianship until they turn 18. And with no will there is no named executor, so the family must apply for a court-appointed administrator and may have to post a bond. Every one of these problems is avoided by a short, properly executed will, at a fraction of what a contested heirship determination at the El Paso County Courthouse costs the family later.

sections.heading: Bilingual Signings and How the Process Works
paragraphs: Many of our estate planning clients are the adult children of parents who are more comfortable in Spanish, and a will the signer does not fully understand is a will that can be challenged. We conduct the consultation and the signing in English or Spanish as the client prefers, explain each document in the language they think in, and make sure the witnesses and notary are present in the room at 11860 Vista Del Sol Dr. — not gathered after the fact. Se habla español, and that is how most signings go.

The process is straightforward. We meet for a free consultation, usually 30 to 45 minutes, to go through family, assets, and what you want to happen. We quote a flat fee at that meeting, draft within about a week, send the documents for review, and schedule the signing. The whole plan — will, durable POA, medical POA, directive and HIPAA release — is typically done within two to three weeks. You leave with the originals and we keep a scanned set.

sections.heading: Flat Fees, Probate, and Which Page to Read Next
paragraphs: Robert Navar quotes flat fees for estate planning after the consultation, once he knows whether the plan is a single will or a married couple's full set with trusts for minor children. For probate, the fee depends on the path: a small estate affidavit under Estates Code Chapter 205 for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead and exempt property, a muniment of title under Chapter 257 when a will exists and there are no debts beyond the mortgage, or a full independent administration when the estate needs an executor with authority to act.

If you need documents for yourself or a parent, start with wills and estate planning. If you are worried about who can make decisions during an illness, read power of attorney and medical directives. If someone has already passed and you are trying to transfer a house, a vehicle or a bank account, go to probate and small estate affidavits. This page is general information, not legal advice about your situation; schedule a free consultation or call 915-503-1600 and we will figure out the right set of documents together.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to write a will in Texas?
faqs.a: Texas allows a handwritten will, but a typed will signed before two witnesses with a self-proving affidavit is far easier to probate and harder to contest. Most probate problems we see start with a do-it-yourself will that was signed wrong or left out independent administration.

faqs.q: What happens to my house in El Paso if I die without a will?
faqs.a: It depends on whether it is community or separate property and whether all your children are also your spouse's. In a blended family the deceased's share of a community-property home passes to the children, not the spouse. A will fixes that with one sentence.

faqs.q: Can you prepare and sign the documents in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. We explain and sign in Spanish for clients who prefer it, with bilingual staff and witnesses present. The documents themselves are prepared in English for the Texas courts, and we walk through every paragraph before anyone signs.

faqs.q: My parent passed away with a small estate. Do we have to go through probate?
faqs.a: Often not. If the estate is $75,000 or less excluding the homestead and exempt property and there is no will, a small estate affidavit under Estates Code Chapter 205 may transfer the assets without administration. If there is a will and no unpaid debts beyond a mortgage, a muniment of title is usually faster than full probate.
